title: Stochastic Voronoi Ensembles for Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper addresses unsupervised anomaly detection on datasets with varying local densities, where distance-based methods miss local anomalies and density-based methods need careful parameters and quadratic time. It proposes SVEAD, which builds an ensemble of t=100 random Voronoi partitions by uniformly sampling m anchors from the data, assigns each point to its nearest anchor, and scores points within each cell by the dual-factor formula (delta/delta_max)*delta_mean, averaged over partitions, giving linear time and constant space. On 45 ADBench datasets SVEAD achieves the best average AUC-ROC (0.8538) and AUC-PR (0.5000) among 13 methods, with per-dataset means and stds over 5 runs reported in Tables 4-7.

match_target.why: User-specified hint. It is cheap (cardio is only 1831x21, CPU-minutes even with the full m-grid x 5 runs) yet comes straight from the paper's primary results table (Table 4, AUC-ROC, the main metric) for the proposed method, showing SVEAD is competitive with isolation-based SOTA on a standard healthcare benchmark (0.9339 vs iNNE 0.9447, IDK 0.9531, iForest 0.9260).

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports a std over repeated runs for the target value (Table 5, cardio, VEAD = 0.0063 over 5 runs); absolute band = 3 x 0.0063 = 0.0189, already at the 4-decimal precision the paper prints.

requirements.stmt: For each of the t partitions, sample m anchors uniformly at random without replacement from the dataset X itself (m << n).
requirements.quote: we randomly sample m points from the dataset X without replacement to form an anchor set

requirements.stmt: Assign every point to its nearest anchor using Euclidean distance, producing m non-overlapping Voronoi cells per partition.
requirements.quote: Each point x ∈X is assigned to its nearest anchor, creating a partition

requirements.stmt: Do not construct an explicit Voronoi diagram; only point-to-cell membership via nearest-anchor queries is computed.
requirements.quote: we do not compute cell boundaries or vertices; we only determine point-to-cell membership through nearest-anchor queries.

requirements.stmt: Score each point within its cell by the dual-factor formula s(x) = (delta/delta_max) * delta_mean, combining relative position normalization with local density weighting.
requirements.quote: where the first term δ/δmax normalizes the distance by the maximum cell radius, and the second term δmean represents the mean distance within the cell.

requirements.stmt: Compute per-cell statistics delta_max (maximum anchor-to-point distance in the cell) and delta_mean (mean anchor-to-point distance in the cell) over the points assigned to each cell.
requirements.quote: computing cell statistics including maximum and mean distances

requirements.stmt: Aggregate the per-partition scores by arithmetic mean over the t partitions to obtain the final anomaly score f(x).
requirements.quote: The final anomaly score is computed as the arithmetic mean:

requirements.stmt: If a cell contains only its anchor (|C_i| = 1), skip scoring that point in that partition and average over the remaining partitions.
requirements.quote: we skip scoring for this point in this partition and rely on the other t −1 partitions in the ensemble average.

requirements.stmt: Use ensemble size t = 100 and select the number of anchors m per dataset by grid search over {2^1, 2^2, ..., 2^8} (printed as {21, 22, . . . , 28}).
requirements.quote: the number of sample points is searched over {21, 22, . . . , 28}, with ensemble size fixed at 100.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate with AUC-ROC (and AUC-PR) in the fully unsupervised setting: labels are used only to compute metrics after prediction, never for training.
requirements.quote: the labels are used to compute the AUC-ROC and AUC-PR for each dataset only after the models have made predictions.

requirements.stmt: Repeat each experiment 5 times and report the mean performance (std reported in Tables 5 and 7).
requirements.quote: For each dataset and method, we repeat experiments 5 times and report the average performance.

requirements.stmt: Use the ADBench benchmark datasets; for the match target, cardio has 1831 samples, 21 features, 176 anomalies (9.61%).
requirements.quote: We evaluate SVEAD on 45 publicly available benchmark datasets widely used in anomaly detection from ADBench (Han et al., 2022).

requirements.stmt: Operate in the unsupervised (contaminated) setting: the input dataset mixes normal and anomalous points and no clean training data or learning procedure is used.
requirements.quote: relying solely on the assumption that anomalies deviate from the majority distribution.
